# Targets and AWS Resource Ownership

**Status**: Authoritative source
**Supersedes**: Pre-refactor substrate/lifetime-class inventory
**Generated sections**: none
**Applicability**: Adopted target projection and ownership contract; current registries are not regenerated by Markdown adoption.

> **Purpose**: Separate retained local management, application targets and test ownership while making the complete cloud deletion scope explicit.

## Management and application targets

| Projection | Placement | Persistent anchor | Deletion contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| Production management | Local kind | `.data/<installation-id>` with exact host extra mounts | Retained by ordinary AWS delete; explicit control removal preserves roots |
| Test management | Separate run-owned local kind | `.test-data/<run-id>` with unique cluster/context/ports | Retire only after the run's cloud/credential cleanup; never reach production |
| Local application | Distinct namespaces/scopes on selected kind | Declared application volumes under that environment root | Component desired-state removal explicit; ordinary AWS delete reports it separately |
| AWS application | Optional EKS controlled only by local Authority | Static owned EBS; owned cloud objects and local journal | Ordinary delete removes complete owned AWS scope and updates retained local state |
| Storage canary | Cheap S3 bucket and versions/markers, not an application cluster | Exact canary identity plus local operation journal | Same shared cloud engine, complete own-family deletion and credential retirement |

The application/platform catalog is the same on local kind and EKS, except the load-balancer, DNS/subzone and block-volume adapters. Management placement is outside that equivalence. See [system components](system-components.md).

## Explicit cloud resource families

| Family | Declared identity/observer | Owner phase | Default delete |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Generated operational IAM principals, roles, policies and keys | Registered exact family/account; real IAM/STS plus independent final verifier | 4 | After all dependants, then retire Vault generations |
| Storage-canary bucket, objects, versions, markers, multipart state | Exact S3 family, service-specific inventory and positive controls | 5 | Remove contents/versions/uploads and owned bucket; no existing aws-test identity reuse |
| Managed DNS records, validation zones and delegated subzones | Exact parent/child coordinates and ownership, not broad zone-name guessing | 7 local support; EKS 8 | Remove owned records/delegation/zones; preserve external parent/domain |
| SES send/receive identities, owned rules, SMTP identities and capture resources | Separate production/test coordinates, exact rule ownership and active-container coordination | 7 | Remove owned SES/S3/IAM/DNS; never keep solely because old class said LongLived |
| Remote Authority/TLS backing stores | Declared owned objects/versions/bucket plus exact IAM scopes | 7 | Preserve local recovery record, remove remote state before its access identity |
| EKS cluster/node groups/Fargate if supported, EC2 and IAM/OIDC | Exact cluster/account/region and registered family manifest | 8 | Quiesce/drain where observable, delete provider resources and read back |
| VPC/subnets/routes/IGW/NAT/endpoints/EIPs | Exact owned VPC and declared network families | 8 | Converge dependants before network roots; no account default-VPC sweep |
| LBC/CNI/CSI/controller children, ENIs/security groups/LBs/target groups | Registered controller family before activation, independently enumerated | 8 | Owner drain plus provider backstops; unknown requester-managed objects are not forced |
| EBS and owned snapshots where created | Static declared PV/volume ownership with production/test data policy | 8 | Both owned test and production cloud data are destructive delete scope under confirmation |
| Registry/cloud logs/images/other support resources when actually created | Explicit catalog entry before effects; no hidden optional-resource exemption | Introducing phase | Complete own lifecycle before introducing phase closes |

Ownership and intended lifetime are distinct. No shared owner is invented during cleanup to evade deletion. Explicitly shared containers retain a declared owner and consumer references from admission; delete releases only this scope's resources/reference unless deleting the owning scope. Non-secret lifecycle metadata remains observable while Vault is sealed; secret payload custody remains protected.

## Credentials and external prerequisites

AWS account, domain, parent hosted zone and temporary operator bootstrap credential are external prerequisites. IAM resource creation uses ephemeral prompt/test-simulator input after local durable admission; subsequent provider work uses narrow generated material in Vault. No ambient auth, host AWS mutation fallback or fixture-to-production config copy is supported.

Tests use distinct identity/SMTP/bucket/DNS/rule coordinates even in a shared AWS account. AWS's active SES receiving rule-set container must be coordinated explicitly; test cleanup cannot deactivate production receiving or remove another owner's rule. Dedicated test accounts are allowed but not a hidden prerequisite for all local phases.

## Retired topology and current availability

The existing `aws-test` program provisions three EC2/RKE2 machines. It is not the Phase 5 S3 canary. New creation of that special target is retired in favor of retained gateway HA objectives on kind/EKS (Phase 9). Exact original-stack diff/adoption/cleanup remains migration-scoped until its actual resources/obligations are resolved (Phase 10).

Current source still contains RKE2, old lifetime classes and generated command/registry artifacts. Do not hand-edit those code-generated tables to pretend implementation. Phase 0 migrates checker/metadata contracts; introducing phases change real adapters and regenerate references. Historical source at `583443f` remains traceable through [history](../documents/history/README.md).
